key_highlights: ASX ended the week lower as traders positioned for higher RBA rates, though the 'bull case returns' narrative offers counterbalance
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical distraction, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
Bathla collapse signals systemic fragility in Australia's construction sector, with ratings agencies warning on Victoria's soaring debt
EV sales surpassed petrol cars for the first time in Australia; BYD confirms EV tipping point reached
Consumer sentiment deteriorating as Australians report feeling poorer amid sticky inflation and housing stress
US jobs data (162k vs 54k expected) strengthens USD, pressuring AUD and commodity-linked ASX names
ASIC launches whistleblower review at Big Four accounting firms, raising governance overhang on financials

sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX (retail) face margin compression; EV supply chain (BYD ecosystem) gains; staples defensive rotation likely

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to modestly lower over 1-3 months as RBA rate expectations dominate. Iron ore weakness and construction sector stress weigh on materials and property. US jobs strength supports global risk appetite but pressures AUD. Bull case narrative (#63) provides floor but rate risk caps upside.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pivots. EV transition, AI infrastructure spend, and gold/battery metals offer structural growth. Construction and housing correction may create value entry points by late 2026. Key risk: prolonged consumer stress and iron ore demand destruction.
